newsitem.title: CHINA: China Aero details CASIL Telecom spinoff.
newsitem.headline: China Aero details CASIL Telecom spinoff.

text.p: China Aerospace International Holdings Ltd said on Thursday its unit CASIL Telecommunications Holdings Ltd proposed to issue 150 million new shares at a price to be announced in a spinoff on the Hong Kong stock market.

China Aerospace said the stock exchange had in principle given an approval for the separate listing. The public offering of the CASIL Telecom issue would run from July 29 to August 1 and dealing in the shares should begin on August 11, it said.
The new issue will represent 25 percent of CASIL Telecom's enlarged share capital, it said.

Of the issue, 30 million CASIL Telecom shares will be preferentially offered to existing shareholders of China Aerospace in the proportion of one CASIL Telecom share for every 25 China Aerospace shares held, the statement said.
Another 7.5 million shares will be made available to employees of CASIL Telecom, it said.

Two Taiwan-related companies had agreed to subscribe for an aggregate 83.94 million shares, or 13.99 percent of the enlarged share capital, at the issue price, it added. One of the strategic investors is CIS Technology Inc, it said.
The strategic investors have undertaken of holding the stake for at least six months from the date of the listing.
Following the spinoff, China Aerospace will hold 61.01 percent of the CASIL Telecom.
A prospectus is expected to be issued on July 29, it said.
Credit Lyonnais Securities (asia) Ltd has been appointed as lead underwriter and sponsor of the new issue.
CASIL Telecom is engaged in telecommunications and global positioning system (GPS) businesses.
Its telecom business consists of development, manufacture, and sales of telecommunications switching equipment and telephone terminal products.
Total sales of the business amounted to HK$262 million for the year ended in December 1996, accounting for 95.7 percent of CASIL Telecom's total sales.
The GPS business, which is carried out in Hong Kong, Macau and in China, consists of development, manufacture, sales and installation of customer-specific GPS application products.
It said those GPS application products are for tracking applications and are built on the CASIL Telecom's Mobile Object Tracking and Control System model.
The GPS business generated HK$12 million in sales revenue for 1996, accounting for 4.3 percent of CASIL Telecom's total sales during the year, the statement said.

The spinoff will provide financial resources for the expansion of CASIL Telecom's business and enabling it become a high technology telecommunications company without requiring its parent to increase gearing funding the expansion, it said.
China Aerospace also said it would focus on the development of its consumer electronics, automobiles, computer software engineering and digital satellite broadcasting businesses after the spinoff.
